title: Novel Method to Analytically Obtain the Asymptotic Stable Equilibria States of Extended SIR-Type Epidemiological Models
short_title: Analytically Obtaining Stable Equilibria of Extended SIR-Type Models
abstract: We present a new analytical method to find the asymptotic stable equilibria states based on the Markov chain technique. We reveal this method on the Susceptible-Infectious-Recovered (SIR)-type epidemiological model that we developed for viral diseases with long-term immunity memory. This is a large-scale model containing 15 nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs), and classical methods have failed to analytically obtain its equilibria. The proposed method is used to conduct a comprehensive analysis by a stochastic representation of the dynamics of the model, followed by finding all asymptotic stable equilibrium states of the model for any values of parameters and initial conditions thanks to the symmetry of the population size over time.
summary: Classical methods failed to analytically find the stable long-term states, known as equilibria, of a large SIR-type epidemic model we developed for viral diseases with long-term immunity memory, which has 15 nonlinear differential equations. We present a new analytical method based on the Markov chain technique, which describes random transitions between states, and use a stochastic representation of the model's dynamics. The method finds all asymptotic stable equilibria for any parameter values and initial conditions.
key_findings: We present a new analytical method based on the Markov chain technique to find asymptotic stable equilibria states.
We apply it to our SIR-type model of viral diseases with long-term immunity memory, which has 15 nonlinear ordinary differential equations.
Classical methods failed to analytically obtain this model's equilibria.
The method finds all asymptotic stable equilibrium states for any parameter values and initial conditions, thanks to population size symmetry over time.
